name: Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI)
source: Five level near-side frames (frames 2-6 at 4 fps from t=17.0 s) from Hammer Strength's official Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI) demonstration video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B27-cHMnlPE&t=17s). Two plates (45 lb + 25 lb, 31.75 kg total) rest on the shared lower loading arm coupled by a single taut flat belt to the upper shaped cam. Force represents combined tangential handle force across both hands on the coupled workarm; sensitivity to the pivoting handle yoke and an independent conservation-of-work check (0.79 kgf/kg) are documented in observation evidence.

observation.evidence: Five level near-side frames (frames 2-6 at 4 fps from t=17.0s, cropped 1080x1080 and resized to 1000x1000) from Hammer Strength's official Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI) demonstration video. The added plates (45 lb + 25 lb = 31.75 kg on the single shared lower loading horn) rotate on the lower load arm around the fixed frame bearing (pivot, near [530, 621]). A single taut flat belt connects the load-arm clevis (belt_load) directly upward to the upper shaped cam (belt_cam), which rotates around the upper cam axle (cam_pivot, near [452, 357], verified to <1.4 px residual by circular-arc fit to the rigid cam-arm rocker pin and matching the center of the circular cam housing). Both hands lift the coupled pivoting handle assembly (grip, marked at the hand contact center on the grip bar); force is total combined tangential hand force across both hands. Camera drift across the five frames is 1-3 px and tracked per frame. Uncertainty: pivot and cam_pivot +/-3 px, belt centerline +/-3-4 px (flat belt edges are brightly lit), plate COM +/-6 px, hand contact +/-6-8 px. Sensitivity check: because the handle yoke pivots freely on the rigid cam-arm rocker pin (R = 200 px around cam_pivot), placing grip at the rocker pin instead of the hand yields 0.70-0.83 kgf/kg (travel-weighted mean 0.77 kgf/kg) compared to 0.62-0.91 kgf/kg (mean 0.81 kgf/kg) at the hand, both closely matching the independent conservation-of-work check over the same five frames (0.79 kgf/kg along the hand path, 0.73 kgf/kg along the handle cap). Anatomical elbow landmarks are omitted because the lifter's elbow is partially occluded behind the black cam housing and the 45 lb plate rim is clipped at the left edge in pose 5.

motion_check.source: Hammer Strength Plate Loaded Seated Biceps demonstration, 1920 × 1080. Near-side view of a single lifting stroke. Original frames have no analysis overlays.
motion_check.extraction: Seek to 17.00 s, apply ffmpeg fps=4 for 5.8 s, use output frames 2–6 (1-based). Crop x=499, y=0, width=1080, height=1080 and resize to 1000 × 1000. Coordinates use top-left origin and y down.
motion_check.landmarks: anchor = near-side load-arm bearing cap. plates = estimated added-mass center between two plates. hand = estimated grip contact hidden by the hand. handle_cap = visible rigid end of the handle. rocker_pin = visible silver pin on the cam rocker.
motion_check.uncertainty: Anchor ±2 px, plate center approximately ±5 to 10 px, hand contact ±8 to 10 px, handle cap ±3 px. This calculation assumes a level, nearly side-on camera and comparable image scales at the hand and plates. The bearing corrects image translation. Parallax, rotating grips, unknown plate mass sharing and the chord approximation affect the result. The handle cap provides a sensitivity check. The rocker pin and grip cap sweep about different apparent centers. The work estimate follows the contact path directly because using grip radius about the cam axle would assume a rigid grip attachment.

base_resistance.source: Hammer Strength lists 2 kg starting resistance per workarm for the PL-BI. The full unloaded curve is unknown. The default holds this force constant across the stroke.
